item.title: He died of 'natural causes.' But his mother says she knows what killed him: heat
item.description: When Arizona counts heat-related deaths, Adam Willson isn't included. His story shows how thousands of heat deaths can go uncounted every year in the United States.
item.content:encoded:
When Arizona counts heat-related deaths, Adam Willson isn't included. His story shows how thousands of heat deaths can go uncounted every year in the United States.

(Image credit: Ryan Kellman)

item.title: NPR spent 2 years tracking deaths from heat. We found a staggering hidden toll
item.description: An NPR investigation found that people in the U.S. are dying from heat much more often than official counts show. We explore the reasons why — and how lives can be saved.
item.content:encoded: An NPR investigation found that people in the U.S. are dying from heat much more often than official counts show. We explore the reasons why — and how lives can be saved.

item.title: A melting glacier contributed to the deadly Nepal floods. We can expect more like this
item.description: As the climate continues to warm, scientists warn that the frequency of disasters like the floods in Nepal will increase.

item.title: Forest service to allow chainsaws to clear trails of downed trees despite ban
item.description: This summer, fallen trees are blocking hundreds of miles of wilderness trails, following unusual weather events. Some forests will allow chainsaws as a controversial exception to a ban on motors.

item.title: The real cause of most wildfires? People
item.description: More than three quarters of all wildfires in the U.S. are caused by human behavior including accidents, negligence and arson.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Spokane wildfire evacuees return home, but it's 'still a hazmat situation'
item.description: Most evacuees have been allowed to return to their homes near burn zones in Spokane, despite concerns about lingering toxins.

item.title: Did climate change cause this heat wave? Most likely, and here's why
item.description: As the senior climate editor at NPR, when extreme weather impacts us, I often send out guidance to the newsroom to help everyone understand the role of climate change. Here's what I tell them.

item.title: Indonesians brave choking smoke to pray for rain as country battles wildfires
item.description: Huge blazes in central and western regions of Indonesia have scorched wide areas of forests and peatland, creating a choking haze that blanketed some cities.

item.title: Drying springs in Arizona jeopardize the future of a key Navajo tradition
item.description: For centuries, Navajo shepherds have herded sheep in Arizona's mountains. Now, springs they rely on are drying up, putting a mainstay of the tribe's culture at risk.

item.title: A new Colorado River plan means big water cuts for some states
item.description: The federal government finally has a new plan for the shrinking Colorado River. With its two biggest reservoirs at record lows, Arizona, California and Nevada will have to make major water cuts.
